\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{noweb}
\noweboptions{smallcode}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\title{Free Time Slots}
\author{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\tableofcontents

\section{Overview}

Given a list of bookings, we want to know when the working day,
08:00--17:00, is still free.  The program is a small pipeline, and each
stage hands the next one a simpler problem:

\begin{description}
\item[Parsing] turns lines such as [[09:00-10:30]] into pairs of minutes
  since midnight.
\item[Merging] collapses overlapping and touching bookings into disjoint
  ones, sorted by start.
\item[Gap finding] walks the merged bookings and reports what lies
  between them inside the working day.
\item[Formatting and I/O] converts minutes back to text and connects the
  pipeline to standard input and output.
\end{description}

The whole program tangles to [[freeslots.py]]; the tests tangle to
[[test_freeslots.py]].

<<[[freeslots.py]]>>=
"""Print the free slots of the working day, given booked slots."""
import re
import sys

<<constants>>
<<functions>>
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
@

<<[[test_freeslots.py]]>>=
import io

import pytest

from freeslots import *


<<test functions>>
@

\section{Parsing}

Working in minutes since midnight turns every later step into plain
integer comparison, so \enquote{does this booking touch that one}
becomes a comparison of two integers.

The day boundaries are constants so that changing opening hours is a
one-line edit.

<<constants>>=
DAY_START = 8 * 60
DAY_END = 17 * 60
SLOT_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*-\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*$")
@

We reject malformed input loudly rather than skipping it: a silently
ignored booking would show up as a falsely free slot, which is the
worst possible failure for a scheduling tool.  Likewise a booking that
ends before it starts is an error, not an empty slot.

<<functions>>=
def parse_slot(line):
    """Return the slot `HH:MM-HH:MM` in `line` as (start, end) minutes.

    Raise `ValueError` if the line is malformed or ends before it starts.
    """
    match = SLOT_RE.match(line)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid slot: {line.strip()!r}")
    h1, m1, h2, m2 = (int(g) for g in match.groups())
    if h1 > 24 or h2 > 24 or m1 > 59 or m2 > 59:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid time in slot: {line.strip()!r}")
    start, end = h1 * 60 + m1, h2 * 60 + m2
    if end < start:
        raise ValueError(f"slot ends before it starts: {line.strip()!r}")
    return start, end
@

Let's verify parsing, including the error cases.

<<test functions>>=
def test_parse_slot():
  assert parse_slot("09:00-10:30") == (540, 630)
  assert parse_slot(" 9:05 - 9:10\n") == (545, 550)

def test_parse_slot_rejects_garbage():
  for bad in ["", "foo", "09:00", "10:00-09:00", "09:60-10:00"]:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
      parse_slot(bad)
@

\section{Merging bookings}

Bookings arrive in any order and may overlap, so we first sort by start.
After sorting, one pass suffices: a booking either begins no later than
the end of the current merged block (it overlaps or touches it, so we
extend the block if needed) or begins strictly after it (so the block is
final, because every later booking starts even later).  Using [[<=]]
rather than [[<]] for the comparison is what makes touching bookings
merge; it is harmless for free-slot output but keeps the merged list
minimal.

<<functions>>=
def merge_slots(slots):
    """Merge overlapping or touching (start, end) slots.

    Return a sorted list of disjoint slots.
    """
    merged = []
    for start, end in sorted(slots):
        if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(merged[-1][1], end))
        else:
            merged.append((start, end))
    return merged
@

<<test functions>>=
def test_merge_unordered_and_overlapping():
  slots = [(600, 700), (540, 620), (800, 900)]
  assert merge_slots(slots) == [(540, 700), (800, 900)]

def test_merge_touching():
  assert merge_slots([(540, 600), (600, 660)]) == [(540, 660)]

def test_merge_contained():
  assert merge_slots([(540, 900), (600, 660)]) == [(540, 900)]

def test_merge_empty():
  assert merge_slots([]) == []
@

\section{Finding the gaps}

With disjoint, sorted bookings the free time is whatever lies between a
cursor and the next booking's start.  The cursor begins at the opening
time and jumps to the end of each booking.  Clipping to the working day
falls out of two [[max]]/[[min]] choices: bookings that end before the
cursor (for instance an early-morning slot) cannot move it backwards,
and a gap is only reported up to [[DAY_END]], so bookings after closing
time add nothing.  Empty gaps are dropped, so back-to-back bookings
produce no zero-length output.

<<functions>>=
def free_slots(booked, day_start=DAY_START, day_end=DAY_END):
    """Return the free (start, end) slots of the day given `booked` slots."""
    free = []
    cursor = day_start
    for start, end in merge_slots(booked):
        if start > cursor:
            free.append((cursor, min(start, day_end)))
        cursor = max(cursor, end)
        if cursor >= day_end:
            break
    if cursor < day_end:
        free.append((cursor, day_end))
    return [(s, e) for s, e in free if s < e]
@

Let's verify the interesting situations: nothing booked, a fully booked
day, bookings poking out of the day on either side, and gaps at the
edges.

<<test functions>>=
def test_free_no_bookings():
  assert free_slots([]) == [(480, 1020)]

def test_free_gaps_between_and_at_edges():
  booked = [(540, 600), (720, 780)]
  assert free_slots(booked) == [(480, 540), (600, 720), (780, 1020)]

def test_free_fully_booked():
  assert free_slots([(480, 1020)]) == []

def test_free_back_to_back_has_no_empty_gap():
  assert free_slots([(480, 600), (600, 1020)]) == []

def test_free_bookings_outside_day_are_clipped():
  booked = [(360, 540), (1000, 1200), (1100, 1200)]
  assert free_slots(booked) == [(540, 1000)]

def test_free_booking_entirely_after_close():
  assert free_slots([(1080, 1140)]) == [(480, 1020)]
@

\section{Formatting and input/output}

The inverse of parsing: [[divmod]] splits minutes into hours and
minutes, and zero-padding keeps the output in the same [[HH:MM-HH:MM]]
shape as the input.

<<functions>>=
def format_slot(slot):
    """Format a (start, end) pair of minutes as `HH:MM-HH:MM`."""
    start, end = slot
    return "%02d:%02d-%02d:%02d" % (*divmod(start, 60), *divmod(end, 60))
@

Blank lines are skipped, since trailing newlines and separators in
piped input are common and carry no booking.  [[main]] takes its streams
as parameters so tests can drive it without touching real standard
input.

<<functions>>=
def main(infile=None, outfile=None):
    """Read bookings from `infile`, print free slots to `outfile`."""
    infile = infile or sys.stdin
    outfile = outfile or sys.stdout
    booked = [parse_slot(line) for line in infile if line.strip()]
    for slot in free_slots(booked):
        print(format_slot(slot), file=outfile)
@

Finally an end-to-end check, with messy input: unordered, overlapping,
touching, and a blank line.

<<test functions>>=
def test_format_slot():
  assert format_slot((480, 545)) == "08:00-09:05"

def test_main_end_to_end():
  stdin = io.StringIO("13:00-14:00\n09:00-10:30\n\n10:00-11:00\n11:00-12:00\n")
  stdout = io.StringIO()
  main(stdin, stdout)
  assert stdout.getvalue().splitlines() == [
    "08:00-09:00",
    "12:00-13:00",
    "14:00-17:00",
  ]
@
